20:1.sourceText: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παύσασθαι τὸν θόρυβον μεταπεμψάμενος ὁ Παῦλος τοὺς μαθητὰς καὶ παρακαλέσας, ἀσπασάμενος ἐξῆλθεν πορεύεσθαι εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
20:1.targetText: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.

groups.note: μετά with the infinitive ("after the uproar ceased") is rendered When … had ended.
The articular infinitive τὸ παύσασθαι ("the ceasing") is rendered had ended.
ἀσπασάμενος ("having taken leave") is rendered he said goodbye to.

20:33.sourceText: ἀργυρίου ἢ χρυσίου ἢ ἱματισμοῦ οὐδενὸς ἐπεθύμησα·
20:33.targetText: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.

groups.note: οὐδενός ("of no one") is rendered not … anyone’s.

20:34.sourceText: αὐτοὶ γινώσκετε ὅτι ταῖς χρείαις μου καὶ τοῖς οὖσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ ὑπηρέτησαν αἱ χεῖρες αὗται.
20:34.targetText: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.

groups.note: τοῖς οὖσιν μετ’ ("those who were with") is rendered companions.
ἐμοῦ ("me"), after μετά ("with"), is rendered my.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds own for emphasis.
English refers back to needs with those.
English adds of mine; the Greek says these hands.

20:35.sourceText: πάντα ὑπέδειξα ὑμῖν, ὅτι οὕτως κοπιῶντας δεῖ ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι τῶν ἀσθενούντων, μνημονεύειν τε τῶν λόγων τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι αὐτὸς εἶπεν Μακάριόν ἐστιν μᾶλλον διδόναι ἢ λαμβάνειν.
20:35.targetText: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”

groups.note: οὕτως ("thus") is rendered by this kind of hard work.
κοπιῶντας ("laboring") is rendered by this kind of hard work.
The article with the participle τῶν ἀσθενούντων ("those who are weak") is rendered the weak.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective τε untranslated; remembering continues the sentence.
BSB introduces the saying with a colon, so ὅτι has no English word.
BSB introduces the saying with a colon and leaves εἶπεν ("He said") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject; δεῖ ("it is necessary") is impersonal (as Acts 5:29).

20:36.sourceText: καὶ ταῦτα εἰπὼν, θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ σὺν πᾶσιν αὐτοῖς προσηύξατο.
20:36.targetText: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.

groups.note: θεὶς τὰ γόνατα αὐτοῦ ("placing his knees") is rendered he knelt down.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse; When renders the participle.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names Paul; the Greek has only the participle εἰπών.
English joins the participle θείς, rendered knelt down, to the main verb prayed.

20:37.sourceText: ἱκανὸς δὲ κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο πάντων, καὶ ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τοῦ Παύλου κατεφίλουν αὐτόν,
20:37.targetText: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.

groups.note: ἱκανός ("considerable"), said of the weeping, is rendered openly.
κλαυθμὸς ἐγένετο ("there was weeping") is rendered wept.
πάντων ("of all") is rendered They all.
BSB renders this καί as as.
ἐπιπεσόντες ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον ("falling on the neck") is rendered they embraced.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἐπιπεσόντες to the main verb; the Greek has no καί here.

20:38.sourceText: ὀδυνώμενοι μάλιστα ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ ᾧ εἰρήκει, ὅτι οὐκέτι μέλλουσιν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ θεωρεῖν. προέπεμπον δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον.
20:38.targetText: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.

groups.note: ᾧ εἰρήκει ("which he had spoken") is rendered his.
οὐκέτι ("no longer") is rendered never … again.
